rulings.quote: according to a predetermined randomized sequence generated using an online-based randomization program (QuickCalcs, GraphPad Software, Boston, MA). | Both study diets were designed and manufactured by Royal Canin SAS (Aimargues, France) with identical packaging but labeled differently for the 2 trial diets with code names “AYC” and “XBZ”.
rulings.rationale: REJECT (the proposer has withdrawn it). Computer-generated block sequence (1.1 Y). Identical, manufacturer-coded diet packs are an accepted equivalent to identical coded containers (1.2 PY). Baseline groups similar apart from ALT (1.3 N). Low, consistent with my earlier ruling. Caveat: only 2 fixed codes, which is weaker than per-animal numbered packs; flagged, not downgraded. Still listed in the updated file; treated as withdrawn per the parent.

rulings.location: PMC11923454 full text, Materials and methods 2.1
rulings.quote: Group allocation was done by one of the researchers (Hilla Chen), using commercial block randomization software (Sealed Envelope), while the owners, attending clinicians, and other researchers were blinded to the treatment administered. | Each dog received either paricalcitol or placebo during the first 12‐week arm, then transitioned to the other treatment for the second 12‐week arm, with a 2‐week washout period between arms. | Depending on the dog's body weight, paricalcitol was either given as 1000 ng Zemplar capsule (EOD) or a 200 ng/mL suspension which was compounded at the hospital's pharmacy by a certified pharmacist. Placebo was given in a capsule or suspension form, respectively.
rulings.rationale: REJECT, resolved explicitly after reading the whole allocation description. The proposer is right that 'Sealed Envelope' is the software name, not sealed envelopes. But concealment does not depend on that phrase. (a) The sequence was computer block randomisation (1.1 Y). (b) Allocation was done by one named researcher, while 'the owners, attending clinicians, and other researchers were blinded', i.e., the people enrolling dogs did not know assignments. (c) Placebo was given in the same capsule/suspension form, compounded by the hospital pharmacist. (d) This is a 2-period crossover (2-week washout): every dog receives both treatments, so a foreseen allocation could only affect sequence order, not which treatment a dog gets. 1.2 PY; 1.3 N (crossover, within-dog). Low; adjudicated_rob_rct.json unchanged. Caveat: the paper does not state whether the allocating researcher also enrolled dogs. A strict reader could call 1.2 NI → S. That would not change Overall (already S via D3/D5).
